verdicts.reason: A reads left to right (can, logo and headline, then CTA), but the legal line is shrunk to an illegible micro-line and the sticker is a tiny smudge jammed next to it under the headline. B has the same legal and sticker problems, and it also puts the CTA first on the far left, so the action comes before the message and the reading order is reversed.

The two are almost identical: can on the left, a two-line headline in the centre, CTA on the right. In both, the legal text is unreadable and the shrunken sticker is crammed against it. A pushes the can closer to the left edge and stretches the illegible legal line wider, so B is marginally better balanced.

A keeps the logical order of product, headline, then CTA, though the CTA sits tight to the right edge and the legal text and sticker are illegible clutter under the headline. B flips the layout so the CTA leads on the left before the brand and headline, which breaks the reading order. It also has the same unreadable fine print and squashed sticker.

A demotes the SOLSTICE logo to a tiny mark at the bottom beside the legal text, which breaks brand prominence. It also puts the CTA first on the left and crowds the bottom with a cramped cluster of logo, illegible legal text and sticker. B keeps the logo above the headline and has a sensible left-to-right flow; its remaining flaws are the unreadable legal line and the tiny sticker.
